data.title: Every 5x5 Nonogram
data.author: eieio
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：5x5非ogram拼图的集体解决游戏及其技术与用户体验问题

不同观点：
• [积极反馈] okayestjoel介绍了他们创建的实时协作非ogram游戏，并提到已经解决了65,000个拼图，邀请大家提供反馈。多个用户（如marssaxman、anxiousbuddhist）表示这个概念很有趣，并赞赏游戏的创意和执行。
• [技术问题] manarth和NooneAtAll3提到游戏中存在服务器通信问题和页面重置问题，影响了用户体验。
• [用户体验问题] Waterluvian和tantalor指出用户界面设计不够直观，难以找到未完成的拼图。anxiousbuddhist建议添加隐藏已完成拼图的功能以改善体验。
• [潜在问题] bspammer和scythe担心有人会使用机器人刷解决量，影响游戏的公平性和趣味性，建议采取措施防止这种行为。

补充讨论：
• [数学与算法] Waterluvian提到所有5x5非ogram无需猜测即可通过算法解决，并认为这是一个有趣的数学现象。
• [扩展想法] x-complexity讨论了将解决的非ogram编码为二进制整数的技术细节，并提出将其用作信息模糊处理的一种形式。butz则分享了自己关于绘制所有可能的8x8像素图标的旧计划，并考虑进一步扩展到2位颜色。
• [不当内容] fph提到可能存在不当内容（如纳粹符号），提醒注意内容审核问题。

争议焦点：
• 游戏的技术问题（服务器通信和页面重置）和用户界面设计是主要争议点，部分用户觉得这些技术问题影响了游戏体验。
• 另一个争议焦点是潜在的不公平行为（如使用机器人刷解决量），用户担心这会破坏游戏的趣味性和公平性。

data.title: Simpler Backoff
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了如何通过使用查找表（lookup table）简化带有指数退避和抖动（jitter）的重试机制代码。初始代码通过循环计算延迟时间并加入随机抖动，而改进后的代码使用预定义的查找表直接列出可能的延迟时间，减少了变量和计算复杂度。这种方法使代码更简洁、易读且易修改，避免了跨循环的逻辑推理和计算错误的风险。文章建议，对于生成少量固定值的场景，应优先使用查找表而不是动态计算。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多种不同的回退（backoff）算法和其实现方式

不同观点：
• **efitz** 支持使用客户端记忆上次回退值并乘以常数的方式，认为这样可以避免查表的复杂性，同时提出加入随机抖动（jitter）以避免客户端同时重试导致的服务器过载问题，并建议服务器端提示随机重试值来缓解服务器重启时的负载压力。
  
• **unsnap_biceps** 认为在较大项目中，不同上游服务需要不同的回退策略，因此倾向于使用算法生成回退时间，而不是为每个服务单独维护查表或多个函数。

• **mukiblejlok** 推荐使用Python的第三方库（stamina）来实现重试机制，认为该库已经包含了讨论中提到的最佳实践，并提供了一个相关视频资源。

• **handsclean** 提出简化回退代码的版本，认为原始代码过于参数化，并建议减少不必要的命名和硬编码，保持代码简洁和灵活。

• **blensor** 认为查表方式不如公式灵活，尤其是当需要修改最大重试次数时，查表方式更繁琐且不易配置。同时指出，查表方式在代码可读性和维护性上不如直接使用公式。

• **axeljohnsson** 提到AWS使用的"自适应重试"策略，强调在系统压力下不应增加负载，这与讨论中提到的抖动（jitter）有相似之处。

• **yawaramin** 提出使用斐波那契回退的个人经验，认为这种方法在某些场景下比指数回退更合适，尤其是在处理长时间等待的场景时。

• **grg0** 建议使用抽象的回退函数（高阶函数）来封装回退逻辑，以便在不同地方复用，而不是为每个场景单独实现。

补充讨论：
• **jelder** 提出是否可以使用迭代器生成器来实现回退逻辑，特别提到了Go语言是否支持该特性，这涉及到更广泛的编程风格讨论。

• **ChrisMarshallNY** 分享了自己在Watch应用中的实现经验，提到使用随机延迟，并指出较新的Watch在这方面的通信更稳定。

• **harpiaharpyja** 认为讨论标题让人以为会涉及不同的回退策略，但实际更多是关于声明式编程风格的讨论。

• **charcircuit** 认为不应偏离大家熟悉的实现方式，否则会适得其反，降低代码可读性。

争议焦点：
• 查表方式 vs. 算法生成回退时间：前者被认为简单但不够灵活，而后者则更具可配置性和适应性。
• 代码简洁性与参数化的平衡：一些评论强调减少不必要的参数化和命名以提高可读性，而另一些则认为必要的参数化可以增加灵活性。

data.title: C++ to Rust Phrasebook
data.author: wcrichton
data.article_summary: 《C++ to Rust Phrasebook》是一本帮助C++程序员学习Rust的书，提供了常见C++模式到Rust习惯用法的转换，通过具体代码示例和工程权衡的高层次讨论进行讲解。本书支持随机访问，适合在编写Rust代码时遇到困惑的情况下查阅。由布朗大学认知工程实验室的专家编写，确保信息的准确性和适度细节，所有内容均为人工撰写，无AI生成。适合有一定Rust基础的读者，也可以作为嵌入式系统程序员的补充资料。读者可以提交反馈或参与问卷调查，帮助改进书籍内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C++与Rust语言的对比及其实践差异

不同观点：
• jpc0认为该指南低估了C++的能力，尤其是在枚举、模块等特性上。他指出，C++通过一些编译器标志和现代工具链也能实现类似Rust的功能，而指南忽视了这些。他还提到Rust的FFI（外部函数接口）在处理图形和FFmpeg等特定领域时不如直接用C++方便。
• EliRivers指出，将一种语言的惯用模式应用于另一种语言可能会导致问题。他以C程序员在C++中使用init()函数为例，说明C程序员需要适应C++的构造函数模式。他还提出，C++程序员在写Rust时需要注意哪些“惯用模式”可能不适用。
• gtani推荐了Drysdale的《Effective Rust》一书，认为它也是针对类似受众的优秀资源。
• amelius观察到Rust版本的代码通常更冗长。
• Animats指出，Rust的traits和C++的类有重大区别，尤其是Rust的traits没有关联数据，也无法访问父trait的数据，这会导致面向对象编程变得混乱。他还提到Rust的所有权模型和错误处理方式与C++显著不同。
• npalli认为，反过来看，这个指南可以帮助C++程序员学习Rust的优点，从而改进C++代码。
• unvalley表示，该指南对没有C++经验的Rust开发者也很有帮助。
• 90s_dev计划利用该指南同时学习Rust和C++，以比较两者的优劣。
• leoh对该指南表示高度赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是C++和Rust在某些特性上的实现和便捷性比较。jpc0认为C++被低估，而Rust在某些方面并不如指南所暗示的那样优越。
• 另一个值得注意的点是Rust的所有权模型和错误处理方式，这些是与C++显著不同的核心概念，可能对习惯C++的开发者构成挑战。
• 不同开发者对指南的用途有不同看法，有人用来学习两种语言，有人用来改进自己对某一种语言的使用。

44140349.article_content:
C++ to Rust Phrasebook
This book is designed to help C++ programmers learn Rust. It provides translations of common C++ patterns into idiomatic Rust. Each pattern is described through concrete code examples along with high-level discussion of engineering trade-offs.
The book can be read front-to-back, but it is designed to be used random-access.
When you are writing Rust code and think, "I know how to do this in C++ but not Rust," then
look for the corresponding chapter in this book.
This book was hand-written by expert C++ and Rust programmers at Brown University's
Cognitive Engineering Lab
. Our goal is provide accurate information with a tasteful degree of detail. No text in this book was written by AI.
If you would like updates on when we add new chapters to this book, you can
drop your email here
.
Other resources
If you have zero Rust experience, you might consider first reading
The Rust Programming
Language
or getting a quick overview at
Learn X in Y Minutes
.
If you are primarily an embedded systems programmer using C or C++, this book is
a complement to
The Embedded Rust Book
.
Compared to resources like the
Rustonomicon
and
Learn Rust With Entirely Too Many Linked Lists
, this book is less about "Rust behind the scenes" and more about explicitly describing how Rust works in terms of C++.
Feedback on this book
At the bottom of every page there is a link
to a form where you can submit feedback: typos, factual errors, or any other issues you spot.
If you answer the quizzes at the end of each chapter, we will save your
responses anonymously for research purposes.
Click here to leave us feedback about this page.

data.title: The Illusion of Causality in Charts
data.author: skadamat
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：图表与因果错觉之间的关系，以及图表可能导致的误解

不同观点：
• gcanyon认为，文章更多讨论的是潜在的因果关系问题，而非图表在误导方面的具体角色。他指出，散点图本身并没有误导性，它只是展示了数据之间的关系，而误解来源于混杂因素（confounding factors）可能导致的数据误读。他希望文章能更多探讨不同类型的图表如何更容易被误解或更具误导性。

• JackSlateur通过提供一个关于虚假相关的链接，暗示图表可能会展示出误导性的相关性，从而让人错误地推导出因果关系。

• nwlotz强调了《如何用统计撒谎》一书的影响，并表达了对信息过载和AI生成图表可能导致的误导性信息的担忧。他担心这些误导性图表会被用作政策制定的依据。

• djoldman认为问题的根源不在于图表本身，而在于人们对图表的解读。他指出，人类天生不善于质疑数据可视化，且容易发现和追随模式。他建议避免使用“因果”相关的词汇，因为这些词汇往往被滥用且容易引起误解。

• justonceokay提出了“统计束缚”谬误的问题，指出将群体统计数据用于描述个体情况是一种误导。他通过举例说明，个体情况可能与群体统计数据有很大差异，且因果关系的方向是从个体到群体，而非相反。

• NoTranslationL分享了一个实际应用中的问题，即在分析个人数据时，人们容易从图表和相关性中得出错误结论。他们的应用Reflect增加了一个实验功能，以帮助用户形成假设并识别混杂变量，从而避免得出错误结论。

• singularity2001指出，因果关系是一个复杂的数学概念，只有极少数人真正理解，但每个人都经常谈论和“使用”它。他强调，虽然人们对因果关系有直觉，但区分相关性和因果关系的细节往往让人困惑。

补充讨论：
• qixv以一种讽刺的方式评论说，混淆相关性和因果关系的人最终都会死去，暗示这种误解可能会带来严重后果。

data.title: AtomVM, the Erlang virtual machine for IoT devices
data.author: ahamez
data.article_summary: AtomVM是Bogdan Erlang抽象机（BEAM）的轻量级实现，可执行从Erlang或Elixir源代码编译的字节码指令。它支持BEAM操作码和Erlang/OTP标准库的精简子集，专为微控制器优化，适用于物联网应用开发。AtomVM具备进程生成、监控、消息传递、抢占式调度和高效垃圾回收等高级功能，并能直接与微控制器的外围设备和协议（如GPIO、I2C、SPI、UART）交互，还支持ESP32等设备的WiFi网络功能。开发成本可低至2美元。相关文档、示例代码和教程正在完善中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AtomVM和其相关技术（如Nerves、Popcorn）在不同平台和设备上的应用，特别是在物联网（IoT）设备和浏览器中的使用，以及与其它虚拟机技术（如JVM）的对比。

不同观点：
• **doawoo**：认为AtomVM非常适合用于MCU（微控制单元）项目的原型设计，相比MicroPython更偏好AtomVM。对于更强大的机器，通常使用Nerves。最近有一个叫Popcorn的项目使用AtomVM在浏览器中运行BEAM VM代码，这为Elixir和Erlang的部署提供了更多可能性。

• **mrbluecoat**：对微型虚拟机工具的激增感到振奋，并分享了一个新的工具链接，显示出对该技术趋势的关注和支持。

• **cyberpunk**：询问AtomVM是否针对比Nerves更小的设备，还是仅仅是Nerves的替代品，表现出对技术定位和适用范围的疑问。

• **thruflo**：提供Popcorn项目的具体信息，指出Popcorn旨在通过WASM运行OTP和Elixir，并分享了一个相关演讲视频链接，帮助澄清Popcorn的功能和目标。

• **svapnil**：质疑Erlang在IoT设备上的实际应用场景，认为Erlang的主要用例更适合强大的机器，表现出对技术适用性的怀疑。

• **amelius**：指出Erlang起源于电信领域，但对移动开发选项的缺乏感到不解，询问该领域未来是否有发展可能性，表现出对Erlang在移动领域应用的关注。

• **lsllc**：认为AtomVM在ESP32上的例子比C语言版本更直接，并强调Erlang的actor模型和潜在的技术优势，特别是如果能够实现OTA更新和代码热加载，表现出对AtomVM技术优势的认可。

• **revskill**：质疑为什么在已有Erlang VM的情况下还要重新发明JVM，并对Java的技术选择和影响提出批评，表现出对技术发展历史的反思和不满。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及的技术包括AtomVM、Nerves、Popcorn、BEAM VM、WASM等，展示了这些技术在不同平台和设备上的应用场景和潜力。
• 争议焦点在于Erlang和AtomVM在IoT设备上的实际应用价值，以及与JVM等其他虚拟机技术的对比，反映了不同技术背景和需求下的观点分歧。
• 讨论还涉及到Erlang在移动和电信领域的发展前景，表现出对该技术未来发展的关注。

44115897.article_content:
AtomVM is a lightweight implementation of the the Bogdan Erlang Abstract Machine (
aka
, the BEAM), a virtual machine that can execute byte-code instructions compiled from Erlang or Elixir source code.  AtomVM supports a limited but functional subset of the BEAM opcodes, and also includes a small subset of the Erlang/OTP standard libraries, all optimized to run on tiny micro-controllers.  With AtomVM, you can write your IoT applications in a functional programming language, using a modern actor-based concurrency model, making them vastly easier to write and understand!
AtomVM includes many advanced features, including process spawning, monitoring, message passing, pre-emptive scheduling, and efficient garbage collection.  It can also interface directly with peripherals and protocols supported on micro-controllers, such as GPIO, I2C, SPI, and UART.  It also supports WiFi networking on devices that support it, such as the Espressif ESP32.   All of this on a device that can cost as little as $2!

data.title: Show HN: AI Peer Reviewer – Multiagent system for scientific manuscript analysis
data.author: rjakob
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为Rigorous的项目，旨在通过透明的、经济高效且快速的人工智能工具改进科学出版过程。项目包括两个主要工具：Agent1_Peer_Review（已完成）提供全面的稿件分析、详细的反馈及生成专业PDF报告；Agent2_Outlet_Fit（开发中）用于评估稿件与目标期刊的契合度。用户可以通过上传稿件并提供相关信息，在1-2个工作日内收到AI生成的评审报告。该项目还提供了详细的PDF报告生成步骤和依赖项说明，所有工具均开源并采用MIT许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI系统在同行评审中的应用及其价值

不同观点：
• **支持观点**：
  - [rjakob] 表示该系统正在接收大量提交，并会在处理完毕后发送报告，同时寻求用户反馈。
  - [hirenj] 认为该工具可以在作者控制的过程中作为检查表，帮助识别 manuscript 中的遗漏，从而提高质量。
  - [karencarits] 对LLM在润色和提供建议方面表示肯定，并期待测试该系统。

• **批评与质疑**：
  - [atrettel] 指出该系统只关注表面问题，如写作质量，而忽略了同行评审中更重要的深层次问题，如工作的创新性。
  - [isoprophlex] 对将原创、重要的未发表研究提交给随机实体表示强烈质疑，认为很少有学者会认为这是个好主意。
  - [deepdarkforest] 强调LLM生成的评审已经充斥在openreview中，真正的评审应来自领域专家，而不是LLM。

• **技术与实现问题**：
  - [davidcbc] 质疑付费版本的附加价值，认为如果系统只是围绕LLM提示的包装，那么其商业模式可能存在问题。
  - [mattmanser] 从编程角度提出了改进建议，包括简化代码结构和优化提示设计，以提高效率和减少错误。

• **使用场景与安全性**：
  - [anticensor] 询问该系统是针对提交前还是提交后的评审，或两者皆可。
  - [eterm] 质疑如果AI代理被视为“同行”，那么是否意味着要接受由AI代理撰写的论文评审。
  - [Syrocce] 提到上传PDF时遇到文件大小限制问题，需压缩后才能成功上传。

补充讨论：
• **时间与效率**：
  - [8organicbits] 对评审延迟表示关注，询问工作日因素如何影响周转时间。
  - [eddythompson80] 希望了解“24个专门代理”的具体含义，以及其复杂性和 sophistication。

• **文化与管理问题**：
  - [eddythompson80] 提到代码评审在快速开发节奏中逐渐失去价值的趋势，管理层往往无法衡量其价值。

争议焦点：
• 该AI系统是否能有效替代或辅助同行评审，尤其是在评估创新性等深层次问题方面。
• 将未发表的研究提交给AI系统进行评审的安全性和学术伦理问题。
• 系统的技术实现和付费版本的附加价值是否合理。

Rigorous - AI-Powered Scientific Manuscript Analysis
Cloud Version Available:
A cloud version of the AI Peer Reviewer is now available at
https://www.rigorous.company/
. Simply upload your manuscript, provide context on target journal and review focus, and receive a comprehensive PDF report via email within 1-2 working days. The cloud version is currently free for testing purposes.
This repository contains tools for making scientific publishing more transparent, cheaper, faster, and ensuring rigorous peer and AI review.
Project Structure
Agent1_Peer_Review
: Advanced peer review system with specialized agents for comprehensive manuscript analysis, detailed feedback, and professional PDF report generation.
Agent2_Outlet_Fit
: (In Development) Tool for evaluating manuscript fit with target journals/conferences.
Current Status
Active Tools
Agent1_Peer_Review
: ✅ Ready for use
Comprehensive manuscript analysis with specialized agents
Detailed feedback on sections, scientific rigor, and writing quality
JSON output with actionable recommendations
PDF report generation (see below)
In Development
Agent2_Outlet_Fit
: 🚧 In Development
Core functionality being implemented
Integration with Agent1_Peer_Review in progress
Testing and validation ongoing
PDF Report Generation
This project includes a PDF report generator that creates a professional peer review report based on the outputs of the review agents.
How to Generate the PDF Report
Ensure you have the required dependencies installed:
reportlab
pillow
(Other dependencies as listed in requirements.txt)
Make sure the following files are present and up to date:
executive_summary.json
(executive summary and overall scores)
quality_control_results.json
(detailed section, rigor, and writing results)
logo.png
(logo for the report header)
Run the PDF generator script:
python Agent1_Peer_Review/pdf_generator.py
The generated PDF will be saved to:
Agent1_Peer_Review/results/review_report.pdf
Features
Cover page with logo, manuscript title, and overall scores
Executive summary and detailed analysis pages for all assessment items (S1–S10, R1–R7, W1–W7)
Visually appealing tables for scores and suggestions
Professional layout, color coding, and consistent formatting
For more details, see the comments in
Agent1_Peer_Review/pdf_generator.py
.
Requirements
Python 3.7+
OpenAI API key
PDF manuscripts to analyze
Dependencies listed in each tool's requirements.txt

data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过API实现盈利和商业模式

不同观点：
• [MasterScrat] 提到他们运营一个文本到图像模型的API，初期通过TPU实现更低成本和更快速度，但现在GPU已赶上，且开源模型的竞争力减弱。目前每月收入约5000美元，比之前减少很多。
• [longnguyen] 分享了一个朋友的案例，他独自运营一个截图API，目前每月经常性收入（MRR）达到20,000美元。
• [tasuki] 表示其公司主要收入来自付费API访问，但面临谷歌等大公司不够精准但够用的竞争压力，并后悔未开发终端用户应用。
• [Simon_O_Rourke] 描述了一个独特的案例：一位前能源公司员工利用对数据库的熟悉，创建API并成功向原公司收费。
• [vsupalov] 指出技术项目的价值往往被低估，因为成功者不愿分享以免引来竞争，并提到24/7视频流服务是一个值得探索的领域。
• [jlundberg] 分享了自己通过SMS和电话API每月收入约500,000欧元，但初期通过线下活动获取客户的模式难以扩展。
• [mtlynch] 提到自己通过一个解析食谱的API每月收入约200美元，但由于使用了RapidAPI，面临高额收费和客户未支付问题。

补充讨论：
• [aaviator42] 提问是否有人希望存在某种API并愿意付费，引发关于潜在市场需求的讨论。
• [tillcarlos] 提到Kraken.io创始人的案例，说明图像处理SaaS的潜在成功。
• [Eikon] 强调证书透明度/子域搜索引擎项目的挑战在于客户获取，而非技术问题。
• [lostmsu] 分享了其语音转文本API的案例，初期通过Reddit评论获取客户，目前每月收入约5000美元。
• [kilroy123] 表示正在尝试通过AI代理实现商业化，但尚未盈利。
• [satvikpendem] 提到Bannerbear等独立开发者年收入至少100万美元的案例，显示该领域的成功潜力。
• [tudorconstantin] 指出区块链API服务商如Infura的成功在于可靠托管区块链服务，尽管早期可以在个人电脑上运行。

争议焦点：
• 开源模型与商业API的竞争力问题：[MasterScrat] 认为开源模型不再具有竞争力，而[vsupalov] 则指出成功者不愿分享，导致社区对商业模式的认知有限。
• 客户获取与市场竞争：多个评论提到获取初始客户和应对大公司竞争是主要挑战。

data.title: Web dev is still fun if you want it to be
data.author: jacques_chester
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者创建一个名为"Best of the Worst"的简单排名系统的经历和感受。作者旨在保持项目的简单性，以自娱娱人为目的，避免现代 web 开发中复杂的团队协作和工具。技术上选择了Sinatra和Sequel，数据库使用SQLite，以求简化开发流程。作者享受这种简单的开发方式，避开了现代前端技术如HTMX，并通过SQL和Ruby简化代码。此外，作者提到AI在编写CSS和节省搜索时间方面有一定帮助，但对它的某些选择感到不满。总体而言，作者通过这个项目重温了2007年时的开发体验，并对此感到愉快。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何在现代 web 开发中找回乐趣与效率，以及对各种工具和框架的评价

不同观点：
• simonw 建议避免使用现代前端构建系统（如 npm/React/TypeScript 等），直接使用 HTML 和 JavaScript 编码，认为这样能重拾开发乐趣，因为现代浏览器 API 已经非常完善，不再需要 jQuery 等库。
• sublinear 强烈反对使用 HTMX，认为它试图解决的问题对小项目和大项目都不适用，且会增加不必要的维护工作，主张严格遵循 web 标准编码，只在项目扩展时适当添加工具。
• iamflimflam1 提到使用 Django 进行初创项目开发，但随着用户对前端交互需求的增加，最终还是需要转向 API 驱动的前端开发，推荐使用 DRF 或 Django-Ninja。
• 29ebJCyy 推荐 Astro，认为它与 Rails 类似，能够在遵循 web 标准的同时提供有趣的 JS 体验，虽然需要重新学习，但值得尝试。
• rsolva 分享了使用 PHP 和简单的 HTML、CSS 构建非营利组织网站的经验，认为这样能避免与他人意见冲突，完全按自己的方式构建网站，带来了极大的乐趣。

补充讨论：
• frankie_t 认为编程的乐趣与工作报酬之间存在冲突，指出许多人认为编程不再有趣是因为他们无法在工作中找到乐趣，只能在业余时间寻找。
• scruple 提到使用 Sinatra 构建个人项目，享受 Ruby 语言和社区的乐趣，但由于工作原因无法在职业中使用。
• nico 强调了通过快速迭代和实验找回编程乐趣，分享了一些小实验项目。
• ofrzeta 提到了 Cloud Foundry 和 Korifi 项目，认为这些技术仍然活跃，并非已经过时。
• pjmlp 主张在 hobby coding 中避免使用现代 JavaScript 构建工具，直接使用 PHP、ASP.NET 或 Spring/Quarkus 等后端技术，并通过直接包含源文件的方式开发 WebGL 或 WebGPU。
• chuckadams 表示不愿意回到 jQuery 和 vanilla JS，认为现代工具如 Vite 虽然设置复杂，但一旦设置好，能带来更好的开发体验和语言优势。
• irrational 提到自己从 90 年代开始做 web 开发，后来因为开发变得不再有趣而退出，但个人项目中仍享受 web 开发的乐趣。
• wwall3r 支持更多初创公司采用简单直接的开发方法，认为这样能提高产品的响应速度和可访问性，但对于需要本地优先的应用，则应从一开始就采用相应技术。

争议焦点：
• HTMX 的使用价值是争议之一，sublinear 认为它增加了不必要的复杂性，而其他人并未直接回应这一观点，但 implicitly 有些人可能不反对使用 HTMX。
• 是否需要现代前端构建工具也是讨论的焦点，simonw 和 chuckadams 站在对立面，前者主张简化开发，后者依赖工具提升开发体验。

The Dumbest Thing I Could Do
This is the repo for the code powering
Best of
Best of the Worst
, a silly, simple ranking system
created purely for my own amusement and the entertainment of other fans. In this README I will outline what I did, how I
did it, and why I did it that way.
Here Begins The Rambling
I don't remember the first time I thought, "shit, I'm old now". But in the dense band of such occasions which thereafter
followed, I know that one such thought was immediately preceded by "gee, developing web apps sucks now". When I was
younger you could follow a problem anywhere it led in the code and solve it, either yourself or with the help of
teammates. But now web dev means teams and committees and tense video meetings and back channel haggling and design
documents at twenty paces. "Depressing" fails to capture the despair this engenders in the way that "bored" incompletely
describes any child after 30 seconds waiting in a line without a screen.
So when I set out to write this little bit of code, I thought: I want to play a bit, sure, but I want to keep it simple.
I'm just pissfarting around here. No need to be formal and fancy. This is for fun, not professional completeness.
And so, by weird coincidence, I stepped into a time machine that zapped me back to 2007. An era so distant that Facebook
was a website and we were still living with the mutant offspring of the 90s and the War on Terror. What happened is that
I made some basic technology choices:
The site needs to be stupidly simple, I don't want a full MVC parade
. OK, I'll use Sinatra.
I guess that rules out Rails, but thank god it also rules out ActiveRecord
. I suppose I'll use Sequel.
I want to use a cheap VPS and my site will get bugger-all traffic
. OK, I'll use SQLite.
SQLite was released in 2000. Sinatra and Sequel were released in 2007. I had fallen into the magic cave and stumbled
out the other side into a world where HTML was the main show and not just a family embarrassment that had to be
stoically, silently endured by React.
Let me tell you. It was wonderful.
Dumb
<form>
s. Why? Because the backend is fast enough that it looks instant. Dumb server-side rendering. Why? Because the
backend is fast enough that it looks instant. Dumb simple slow friendly Ruby code. Why? Because computers are somewhere
between a bajillion and a hojillion times faster than they were when I first rented at VPS (in 2007, as it so happens).
Hyperlinks. Tiny data. Total network traffic under 200k per page. Two threads for two cores. It was enough.
I even eschewed HTMX. I bought the book! It's great, it made me feel hopeful, I want to use it someday. But I just ...
didn't need it. This is a dumb simple site. The interactive vibe is an illusion bred by being simple and light and dumb.
Some Decisions
I like SQL. It is neat. It is powerful. I will use it to simplify the Ruby code. Until LLMs came along query planners
were the closest thing we had to magic.
I like Ruby too. A lot, it's my happy place, I come back to it a lot. I actually tried writing the first version of
this thing in Java, a fine upstanding language with many influential friends. I first took a crack at Helidon because I
was curious what it was like (tl;dr, it's ragged). Then switched to Spring because I've used it in the past and it has
all the sprockets and wheels and zip-zap doodads anyone could wish for. But I ran headfirst into the problem of
deploying it. Have you ever tried deploying Java apps without getting a PhD? It's like asking Satan to underwrite your
home loan when his nuts are itchy. Ruby is just some text. It used to be a PITA because it wasn't an Apache in-process
thing like PHP, but now it's fast enough by itself that it doesn't matter. Boo Satan. Yay Ruby. Also: bring back Cloud
Foundry.
Speaking of AI, is it any use? Well, somewhat. It writes half-useful CSS. It saves time on some things (but also makes
bizarre choices on other things -- whatevs). I basically paired with it occasionally. It was OK. Saved a few episodes of
Midsommer Google Searches
. It drafted the first version of the "about" page, which I mostly rewrote. Who in their
sane earthly mind still writes "Questions? Suggestions?" or "Crowdsourced" in this the year of our flying zombie two
thousand and twenty five? Nobody except an absurdly self-confident fog of floats, that's who.

data.title: Show HN: PunchCard Key Backup
data.author: ciprian_craciun
data.article_summary: 该项目名为“punchcard-key-backup”，旨在通过打孔卡的方式将128位信息备份到物理介质中。用户可以通过项目网页输入或随机生成128位数据，获得打孔图案，并使用铝片、打孔工具等简单工具制作备份卡片。恢复数据时，只需根据卡片上的孔洞图案在网页上选择对应选项，即可还原原始数据。项目提供自包含的HTML文件，不依赖外部资源，所有资源嵌入HTML中。用户也可以通过Python脚本手动生成和恢复数据。该方法不提供冗余，但使用坚固材料如不锈钢可增强耐久性。项目代码和文档采用CC BY 4.0许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过打孔金属板存储加密信息的方案及其优缺点

不同观点：
• [im_down_w_otp] 表示非常喜欢这个方案，并计划将其应用于自己的数控 router，以便按需生成这些金属板。
• [yencabulator] 推荐了一个相关项目 "paperback"，并提供了一个视频链接，供参考。
• [cypherpunks01] 提出使用更密集的256位卡存储完整年龄密钥，并通过金属钥匙非对称加密任意数量的数据，同时建议使用 "sops" 进行阈值处理，以实现 M of N 备份解密。
• [neilv] 欣赏方案的生存能力和手工工具可行性，但建议使用数字和字母印章或激光切割以提高信息密度和可读性。
• [rubyfan] 联想到军队中使用的非长期保存的纸条钥匙，可以像任务 impossible 一样焚烧。
• [G_o_D] 提出通过刷漆或暗房技术打印孔洞，并建议通过分割金属板或叠加掩码板实现更复杂的加密方法。
• [QuadrupleA] 质疑是否打印QR码更简单，并认为如果只是为了复古趣味可以继续。
• [throwanem] 提醒注意存储环境的电化学影响，建议避免不同金属接触等问题。
• [kens] 质疑128位的容量，期望打孔卡能容纳更多信息。
• [kristianp] 欣赏方案的Python代码简洁性，并提供了一个示例。
• [noman-land] 提到Cryptosteel作为类似产品，但未被其他人提及。
• [thih9] 担心长时间后会忘记解码方法，建议直接雕刻常规字符更简单。
• [Mraedis] 觉得方案愚蠢但有趣，个人更倾向于直接在石板上打印文字。
• [msk-lywenn] 认为这个方案像新的二维条码，质疑为何不直接使用有冗余的QR码。
• [deadbabe] 建议开发一个用户界面，以便更快输入1和0，而不是点击复选框。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：方案的实用性与复杂性之间的平衡。部分人认为直接使用现有技术如QR码更简单，而其他人则欣赏方案的创意和手工操作的趣味。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：包括存储环境的考虑、信息密度和可读性的提升、以及不同加密方法的实现和安全性讨论。

pckb -- PunchCard Key Backup
About
This small project
-- available live at
https://volution.ro/pckb
(or
https://purl.org/999
for long term permanence)
-- allows one to take any 128 bits of information,
and easily create
(
and especially easily recover
)
a backup of it into a physical medium,
by using the old and tried method of
punched cards
(hence the project's name).
For example,
the 128 bit number represented in hexadecimal as
d74ae47dc6f599d3f9cb847bd77d6b7c
,
can be backed up as the following standard (CR80 ID) card sized aluminium sheet,
which can then be put into a safe place:
All of this can be achieved by anyone at home, with access only to the following:
using the self-contained HTML at the link above (
https://volution.ro/pckb
),
either by entering the data manually, or by generating random data,
one can get the hole punching pattern;
(this whole procedure is described in the
help
,
and you could consult it for more details;)
from the same link above, or from
here
,
one can print a standard (CR80 ID) card sized stencil,
to be used as a guide for the hole punching;
a small sheet of aluminium;
(I've used a 0.5mm thick one I've bought from the hardware store for ~4 EUR;)
a
punch tool
,
used to mark (with the help of the stencil)
where the holes should be punched;
a small drill,
used to actually punch the holes;
(I've used a 1.00mm drill bit adapted to a standard screwdriver;)
a cutter, to cut the aluminium steel sheet to the standard (CR80 ID) card size;
(I've just used a ruler, and passed the cutter multiple times over the aluminium sheet,
and in the end, it passed through;)
(obviously, one can just use a wood plank, nail, and rock;)  :)
The recovery is as simple as:
use the same self-contained HTML at the link above;
make sure the checkboxes follow the punched holes pattern (for the key);
check that the CRC checkboxes match the punched holes pattern (for the CRC);
recover the base 10, hexadecimal, or text representation of the backendup information;
Alternatively, without any software,
just use simple binary to decimal (or other base) conversion as described
on Wikipedia
.
FAQ (Frequently asked questions)
How can I trust the HTML you've provided?
You can (and should) save it locally, and use it from your computer.
It doesn't load any external resources.
None;  even the images and attachments are saved as
data:
URIs,
thus embedded into the HTML itself.
Do I even need the HTML you've provided?
You don't.
This is just one possible implementation,
mainly meant for experimentation.
You can easily just write the following snippet to generate the bit pattern:
python -c '_secret = "d74ae47dc6f599d3f9cb847bd77d6b7c" ; print (bin(int(_secret,16))[2:])'
And, for the reverse just write the following snippet:
python -c '_bits = "11010111010010101110010001111101110001101111010110011001110100111111100111001011100001000111101111010111011111010110101101111100" ; print (("%032x"%int(_bits,2)))'
What if I have more than 128 bits to save?
Use a cryptographic tool such as
https://github.com/FiloSottile/age
or
https://github.com/gpg/gnupg
to encrypt your secret data with a random 128 bit password (encoded into hexadecimal),
then backup the password as described above (by using the
key hex
input field),
and mirror your encrypted data to family and friends.
How much redundancy is there in the resulting backup?
None, besides the 16 bits of CRC.
However,
by using sturdy materials
(such as a thick stainless steel sheet),
there shouldn't be much need for redundancy.
Does it support secret sharing?
This is in fact, just a digital-to-physical-medium encoding scheme,
thus with enough imagination, it can support secret sharing.
See the Wikipedia page about
secret sharing
for possible ideas.

44145202.article_summary: 该项目名为“punchcard-key-backup”，旨在通过打孔卡的方式将128位信息备份到物理介质中。用户可以通过项目网页输入或随机生成128位数据，获得打孔图案，并使用铝片、打孔工具等简单工具制作备份卡片。恢复数据时，只需根据卡片上的孔洞图案在网页上选择对应选项，即可还原原始数据。项目提供自包含的HTML文件，不依赖外部资源，所有资源嵌入HTML中。用户也可以通过Python脚本手动生成和恢复数据。该方法不提供冗余，但使用坚固材料如不锈钢可增强耐久性。项目代码和文档采用CC BY 4.0许可证。

data.title: A Lean companion to Analysis I
data.author: jeremyscanvic
data.article_summary: 作者大约20年前编写了《Analysis I》这本实分析教材，专注于基础问题，如自然数、整数、有理数和实数的构造，以及提供足够的集合论和逻辑知识以帮助学生进行严谨的证明。虽然编写时未考虑形式化验证，但随着对证明助手的了解，作者意识到该书内容与Lead等证明助手兼容。因此，作者推出了《Analysis I》的Lead配套项目，将书中的定义、定理和练习“翻译”成Lead代码，允许通过填补代码中的“sorries”来完成练习。该项目目前已翻译了部分章节，并有意在后续章节中更多依赖Lean的Mathlib库。作者欢迎志愿者测试该项目并提供反馈，以确保练习能在Lead中顺利完成。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用Lean进行数学教学的优点、挑战以及相关资源和工具的比较

不同观点：
• **立即反馈的优势**：ubj认为Lean的编译器可以提供即时反馈，这比等待人工反馈更有效率，并建议未来可以提供更具指导性的反馈，类似于Rust编译器的建议功能。
• **学习曲线的挑战**：danabramov和brosco认为Lean和Mathlib的学习曲线较陡，尤其是Mathlib的复杂性可能对初学者造成困难，但同时他们也认为这是将数学书籍与工具连接起来的有益尝试。
• **工具选择的理由不明确**：thdhhghgbhy指出作者未详细解释为何选择Lean而非Coq或Agda。
• **数学教育的激进观点**：UltraSane主张数学教育应侧重于计算机代数系统和定理证明器的构建，强调实用性和可视化，而非传统的纸笔计算。
• **教材与形式化证明的对比**：jhanschoo担心Mathlib中使用的过滤器概念与传统教材中的epsilon-delta方法存在差异，可能会对教学造成困扰。
• **资源和项目的分享**：IssaRice列举了多个尝试将Tao的Analysis I形式化到Lean的项目和资源，指出了这些项目大多停留在前几章，并分享了相关的GitHub链接。

补充讨论：
• **Lean在不同数学领域的应用**：nextos提到定理证明在编程语言理论中已有应用，并认为分析中的定理相对更难，建议从 simpler starting point 开始。
• **Lean在主流教材与形式化数学库中的比较**：zozbot234讨论了主流教材与Mathlib在教授实分析时的不同方法，并提出了是否应在学术课程中教授Mathlib版本的问题。
• **具体领域的学习资源**：331c8c71询问使用Lean学习线性代数的起点，westurner则提到HoTT（同伦类型论）作为数学基础的替代方案，并分享了相关资源。
• ** isomorphism 的相关性**：practal质疑证明 isomorphism 到Mathlib等价的重要性，并询问是否可以省略这一部分。

争议焦点：
• **Mathlib的复杂性与教学适用性**：一部分讨论者认为Mathlib的复杂性和快速变化可能不适合作为教学工具，而另一部分讨论者则认为这是一种有益的挑战和学习机会。
• **工具选择的理由**：部分讨论者对选择Lean而非其他定理证明器表示疑惑，认为需要更明确的解释。

总结：讨论围绕使用Lean进行数学教学的优缺点展开，涉及学习资源的分享、工具选择的合理性以及具体教学方法的适用性等问题。

44145517.article_content:
Almost 20 years ago, I wrote a textbook in real analysis called “
Analysis I
“. It was intended to complement the many good available analysis textbooks out there by focusing more on foundational issues, such as the construction of the natural numbers, integers, rational numbers, and reals, as well as providing enough set theory and logic to allow students to develop proofs at high levels of rigor.
While some proof assistants such as Coq or Agda were well established when the book was written, formal verification was not on my radar at the time. However, now that I have had some experience with this subject, I realize that the content of this book is in fact very compatible with such proof assistants; in particular, the ‘naive type theory’ that I was implicitly using to do things like construct the standard number systems, dovetails well with the dependent type theory of Lean (which, among other things, has excellent support for quotient types).
I have therefore decided to launch a
Lean companion to “Analysis I”
, which is a “translation” of many of the definitions, theorems, and exercises of the text into Lean. In particular, this gives an alternate way to perform the exercises in the book, by instead filling in the corresponding “sorries” in the Lean code. (I do not however plan on hosting “official” solutions to the exercises in this companion; instead, feel free to create forks of the repository in which these sorries are filled in.)
Currently, the following sections of the text have been translated into Lean:
Section 2.1: The natural numbers
Section 2.2: Addition
Section 2.3: Multiplication
Chapter 2 epilogue: Isomorphism with the Mathlib natural numbers
Section 3.1: Basic set theory
Section 4.1: The integers
The formalization has been deliberately designed to be separate from the standard Lean math library
Mathlib
at some places, but reliant on it at others. For instance, Mathlib already has a standard notion of the natural numbers
. In the Lean formalization, I first develop “by hand” an alternate construction
Chapter2.Nat
of the natural numbers (or just
Nat
, if one is working in the
Chapter2
namespace), setting up many of the basic results about these alternate natural numbers which parallel similar lemmas about
that are already in Mathlib (but with many of these lemmas set as exercises to the reader, with the proofs currently replaced with “sorries”). Then, in an epilogue section, isomorphisms between these alternate natural numbers and the Mathlib natural numbers are established (or more precisely, set as exercises). From that point on, the Chapter 2 natural numbers are deprecated, and the Mathlib natural numbers are used instead. I intend to continue this general pattern throughout the book, so that as one advances into later chapters, one increasingly relies on Mathlib’s definitions and functions, rather than directly referring to any counterparts from earlier chapters. As such, this companion could also be used as an introduction to Lean and Mathlib as well as to real analysis (somewhat in the spirit of the “
Natural number game
“, which in fact has significant thematic overlap with Chapter 2 of my text).
(One technical note: for my own convenience, I have placed this companion as a subdirectory of another one of my repositories, which was aimed at formalizing the theory of orders of magnitude discussed in
this previous blog post
. I may eventually split off this companion into its own repository, but at this stage I think it is workable to host two largely independent projects in the same repository.)
The code in this repository compiles in Lean, but I have not tested whether all of the (numerous) “sorries” in the code can actually be filled (i.e., if all the exercises can actually be solved in Lean). I would be interested in having volunteers “playtest” the companion to see if this can actually be done (and if the helper lemmas or “API” provided in the Lean files are sufficient to fill in the sorries in a conceptually straightforward manner without having to rely on more esoteric Lean programming techniques). Any other feedback will of course also be welcome.

data.title: Oxfordshire clock still keeping village on time after 500 years
data.article_summary: 东亨德雷德村的圣奥古斯丁教堂钟楼时钟已运行500年，被认为是英国最古老的仍在原址运行的时钟之一。该时钟没有钟面，通过教堂钟声每刻报时，并通过一个类似巨大音乐盒的装置每天四次播放曲子。2015年，时钟因故障停摆，经过修复和安装自动上弦系统后恢复运行。本周，村民们庆祝了时钟500周年，并有机会参观其运行机制。尽管受天气影响，时钟的精准度在历史上相当出色。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：村庄教堂钟声的历史、功能及其与社区生活的关系

不同观点：
• [alfanick] 描述了瑞士小村庄教堂钟声的具体情况，包括每小时报时、每15分钟响一次钟以及早晨6点的“唤醒铃”。最初可能让人感到厌烦，但最终人们习惯并利用钟声判断时间。
• [Daub] 补充了历史背景，指出在铁路出现之前，不同村庄可能有各自的“时区”，由教堂钟表定义。铁路的发展终结了这一现象。
• [pm215] 提供了2014年钟表运作视频链接，展示了钟表在修复前的情况。
• [eleveriven] 认为钟声与日常生活和社区紧密相连，这种联系让人感到温馨。
• [Archelaos] 提到萨利斯堡大教堂展示的1386年钟，提供了一个历史实例。
• [julian55] 分享了自己村庄中类似但可能不那么古老的钟表。
• [layer8] 和 [mattgrice] 对钟表的准确性表示赞赏，认为其功能已经满足需求。
• [mike-the-mikado] 提供了有关行政区划变动的历史信息，指出该村庄在1974年前属于不同的郡。
• [cnewey] 意外地在自己村庄看到相关讨论，并分享了个人经历，提到早上9点钟声正好响起。
• [smitty1e] 以幽默的方式讨论了钟表的升级，提到机械化卷绕系统的安装，结束了人工每天爬楼梯上钟表室的需要。
• [madaxe_again] 对钟表机制的年代提出质疑，认为虽然框架可能是16世纪的，但其余部分可能来自更晚的修复时期，并指出这种技术演变体现了钟表技术的连续性和稀有性。
• [sagarpatil] 简单指出钟表比美国历史更悠久。
• [swayvil] 喜欢钟表机械的规模，认为其易于管理。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及了钟表的历史演变和技术升级，以及其在社区中的功能和象征意义。

44122860.article_content:
Clock still keeping village on time after 500 years
4 days ago
Share
Save
Joe Campbell
BBC News
Share
Save
BBC
St Augustine's clock in East Hendred has been keeping time since Henry VIII was on the throne.
Villagers have been celebrating the 500th birthday of the clock in their parish church.
The timepiece in East Hendred, near Wantage in rural Oxfordshire, is believed to be one of the oldest clocks in Britain still in its original location.
With no clock face or hands, it relies on the church bells in the tower at St Augustine's to ring out the time every quarter hour.
The decision to install it in the church was taken when Henry VIII was on the throne, explained the man responsible for St Augustine's bells, Tower Captain Nigel Findley.
"Imagine the excitement that would have caused then," he said.
The clock is linked to a carillon which uses winches and pulleys to drive hammers high above that strike the bells every quarter hour.
As well as striking the bells every quarter hour, a carillon resembling the insides of a giant musical box, plays a tune called Angel's Song four times a day, every three hours, starting at 09:00.
In 2015, one of the hammers used to strike the six bells came away and fell into the mechanism, jamming it and silencing the clock.
"It was like missing a friend," said church council secretary Ann Pappenheim. "It's a real part of living in the village.
"When you're working in the garden, it really does give you a sense of time and I missed it," she added. "Now it's back and it's wonderful."
The clock, which was originally built a few miles away in Wantage, underwent a lengthy renovation.
A modification also saw the installation of a mechanised winding system, ending the requirement for somebody to climb the narrow, winding staircase each day to the clock room to do the job by hand.
With no clock face on the tower the timepiece relies on the church bells to signal the time
This week, to mark the clock's birthday, people were able to visit the tower to see the mechanism in action.
Acting as guide was Simon Gilchrist, who led the restoration.
He described it as being "a real passion," to have spent time on the project.
"It's not often that we as clock repairers get the opportunity to work on something that is old, but also something that is of great historical importance," he said.
The clock used to be set using a sundial on the outside of the tower. Now a modern digital clock secured to the wall, next to the Tudor era mechanism is used.
"When this thing was made 500 years ago, we didn't have the accuracy that we have today," said Mr Gilchrist.
Parts of the mechanism like the pendulum expand in the summers heat and contract in the cold of winter, all affecting timekeeping.
This was a device built for a time when peoples' days began at dawn and ended shortly after the sun went down.
Given that, he added: "In terms if accuracy, it's pretty accurate."

Designing Pareto-optimal GenAI workflows with syftr
You’re not short on tools. Or models. Or frameworks.
What you’re short on is a principled way to use them —
at scale.
Building effective generative AI workflows, especially agentic ones, means navigating a combinatorial explosion of choices.
Every new retriever, prompt strategy, text splitter, embedding model, or synthesizing LLM multiplies the space of possible workflows, resulting in a search space with over 10²³ possible configurations.
Trial-and-error doesn’t scale. And model-level benchmarks don’t reflect how components behave when stitched into full systems.
That’s why we built syftr
— an open source framework for automatically identifying Pareto-optimal workflows across accuracy, cost, and latency constraints.
See syftr in action
Want a quick walkthrough before diving in? This short demo shows how syftr works to help AI teams efficiently explore generative AI workflow configurations and surface high-performing options.
The complexity behind generative AI workflows
To illustrate how quickly complexity compounds, consider even a relatively simple RAG pipeline like the one shown in Figure 1.
Each component—retriever, prompt strategy, embedding model, text splitter, synthesizing LLM—requires careful selection and tuning. And beyond those decisions, there’s an expanding landscape of end-to-end workflow strategies, from single-agent workflows like
ReAct
and
LATS
to multi-agent workflows like
CaptainAgent
and
Magentic-One
.
Figure 1
. Even a simple AI workflow requires selecting and testing multiple components and hyperparameters.
What’s missing is a scalable, principled way to explore this configuration space.
That’s where
syftr
comes in.
Its open source framework uses multi-objective
Bayesian Optimization
to efficiently search for Pareto-optimal RAG workflows, balancing cost, accuracy, and latency across configurations that would be impossible to test manually.
Benchmarking Pareto-optimal workflows with syftr
Once syftr is applied to a workflow configuration space, it surfaces candidate pipelines that achieve strong tradeoffs across key performance metrics.
The example below shows syftr’s output on the CRAG (Comprehensive RAG) Sports benchmark, highlighting workflows that maintain high accuracy while significantly reducing cost.
Figure 2
. syftr searches across a large workflow configuration space to identify Pareto-optimal RAG workflows — agentic and non-agentic — that balance accuracy and cost. On the
CRAG Sports benchmark
, syftr identifies workflows that match the accuracy of top-performing configurations while reducing cost by nearly two orders of magnitude.
While Figure 2 shows what syftr can deliver, it’s equally important to understand how those results are achieved.
At the core of syftr is a multi-objective search process designed to efficiently navigate vast workflow configuration spaces. The framework prioritizes both performance and computational efficiency – essential requirements for real-world experimentation at scale.
Figure 3.
syftr uses multi-objective Bayesian Optimization (BO) to search across a space of approximately 10²³ unique workflows.
Since evaluating every workflow in this space isn’t feasible, we typically evaluate around 500 workflows per run.
To make this process even more efficient, syftr includes a novel early stopping mechanism —
Pareto Pruner
— which halts evaluation of workflows that are unlikely to improve the Pareto frontier. This significantly reduces computational cost and search time while preserving result quality.
Why current benchmarks aren’t enough
While model benchmarks, like
MMLU
,
LiveBench
,
Chatbot Arena
, and the
Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard
, have advanced our understanding of isolated model capabilities, foundation models rarely operate alone in real-world production environments.
Instead, they’re typically one component — albeit an essential one — within larger, sophisticated AI systems.
Measuring intrinsic model performance is critical, but it leaves open critical system-level questions:
How do you construct a workflow that meets task-specific goals for accuracy, latency, and cost?
Which models should you use—and in which parts of the pipeline?
syftr addresses this gap by enabling automated, multi-objective evaluation across entire workflows.
It captures nuanced tradeoffs that emerge only when components interact within a broader pipeline, and systematically explores configuration spaces that are otherwise impractical to evaluate manually.
Inspiration and related work
syftr is the first open-source framework specifically designed to automatically identify Pareto-optimal generative AI workflows that balance multiple competing objectives simultaneously — not just accuracy, but latency and cost as well.

44144308.article_content:
Using ed(1) as My Static Site Generator
By Artyom Bologov
I have a long story with bipolar spikes making me re-evaluate my tech choices.
You can observe it with multiple of my website setups:
I started with Tripod, my Gemtext-oriented OOP Lisp engine
.
Then I used the DSLs Common Lisp provides to generate HTML from s-expressions
.
And, finally, I switched to C Preprocessor
.
And here's a new flare-up, I guess?
This time I'm testing the limits of what ed-family editors can do.
Including parsing Lisp
.
And using ed as an everyday scripting environment
.
I've also tried ex/vi (not Vim!)
To the point of making a Lisp programming config for it
.
But ex/vi are too troublesome, so forget it
.
Back to ed then!
Here's a compiler from high-level Modal system to ed, written in ed itself
.
Here's a script processing Wisp syntax extension for Lisps
.
And here's a whole category for ed tasks I solved on RosettaCode
.
The overarching narrative can be a transformation from one format to the other.
Like... what site generators do?
So I can use ed as my site generator, and get away with it?
Setup: Glorified ed Scripts
#
So the way ed scripts are ran:
ed -s file.html < script.ed
Example script run
This incantation
Opens a
file.html
,
Reads commands from stdin (redirected
script.ed
.)
And saves/writes (
w
command) file if there are respective commands in the stdin.
A huge advantage is that I can swap commands in the script file.
Replacing writing commands to printing ones, for example.
This way, I can print the content of the post without modifying it.
Y'know, for blog debugging (everyone does that?)
With that general formula, I can abstract article builds per format with two scripts:
a preprocessing (deabbreviation and escaped char expansion) script and the actual conversion.
Here's how
my Makefile rule for .txt building
looks like:
%.txt: %.h
-cp $^ $@
-ed -s $@ <
scripts/preprocess.ed
-ed -s $@ <
scripts/totxt.ed
Makefile implicit rule for conversion from .h to actual output text files
Repeat this for every format (my site supports five atm) with dedicated
to*.ed
scripts.
And that's it!
Advantages
#
I can use whatever syntax I want now!
With C Preprocessor, I was restricted to
X(ARG1, ARG2, ...)
structure for all my elements.
With ed, I can go crazy with something like
<cd code-here>
, imitating self-closing HTML tags.
Or whatever.
Closer to the way I model my writing.
Another upside: I don't have to rewrite all of my posts in a new format.
My ed scripts are processing the old preprocessor-oriented format too!
So ed is capable of replacing C Preprocessor and even adds some features on top.
One more advantage is that there no longer are weird chars breaking everything.
When I see an apostrophe, my eye starts twitching.
C Preprocessor recognizes apostrophe as a char marker and reads the rest of the line verbatim.
Same goes for double quote and hash.
Special chars, forbidden magic.
In general, ed has this sloppiness of regex/substitutions.
And interactivity of a REPL (well, to an extent.)
Perfect for text processing and document authoring.
Limitations
#
ed is stupid (I say lovingly.)
It has no file inclusion, for one.
So C Preprocessor's
#include
is no longer accessible.
I manage without it, because most of the files I include are easily hard-codeable.
But the mere inability to include arbitrary files is somewhat alarming.
Another problem that I already got the taste of:
having arbitrary substitutions at the fingertips spoils me.
I might end up with some really otherworldly syntax without noticing.
And I wouldn't be able to rollback to e.g. C Preprocessor to generate my posts.
But then, ed is so simple and more or less standard, so what can go wrong?
It did go wrong
Arch and Alpine package slightly different versions of ed.
Alpine version was breaking on line joining and variable substitution.
So I had to swap Alpine for Arch on the Gitlab CI.
I would have been able to stay on Alpine if I was able to debug what's wrong with ed there.
But Gitlab (like any other CI platform?) doesn't make it easy to debug things on CI.
Should You Use ed As Site Generator?
#
No, not at all.
It's a weird choice that's only there because I'm having a new phase.
But still, it's fun!
Try ed if you have too much free time and are bored out of your mind 😜
Leave feedback! (via email)

data.title: Sguaba: Hard-to-misuse rigid body transforms for engineers
data.author: lukastyrychtr
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一个名为Sguaba的Rust库，旨在简化处理不同坐标系之间转换的过程，特别是针对工程师而非数学专家。Sguaba通过强类型系统避免不同坐标系间的混淆，支持如WGS84、ECEF、NED、FRD等坐标系，并提供这些系统之间的转换功能。它利用Rust的类型系统防止错误使用，并附有详细文档解释理论和实践。文章通过一个飞行员观察物体位置的示例，展示了如何使用Sguaba在不同坐标系间进行转换，强调了安全构造转换的重要性。Sguaba的目标是让工程师专注于其他重要任务，而不必深究线性代数细节。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• [fsloth] 支持强类型坐标系统，认为通过强类型来区分不同坐标系可以有效避免许多潜在的错误。他建议为不同坐标系创建特定类型，并实现所需的代数运算，从而提高代码的健壮性。
• [techbro92] 表示曾遇到由于向量在错误坐标系中表达而导致的细微错误，认为类似强类型方案值得考虑。
• [kaibee] 通过在游戏开发中的实际经验证实了强类型向量的优势，并提到使用AI生成C#代码，实现了类型安全的Vector3，从而节省了大量时间。
• [avs733] 认为这种强类型方案在航空航天等行业推广时会遇到验证问题，因为这些行业更关注系统的稳定性和历史遗留代码（如MATLAB和Fortran）。他还提出可变精度类型的选项可能是一个有趣的补充。

• 关于Rust语言设计的问题，提出了对基本数据类型和错误处理的关注，反映出语言设计早期决策对后续开发的影响。

争议焦点：
• 强类型坐标系统在不同行业中的实际应用价值和推广难度。
• 新增Rust库的必要性及其对几何处理的影响。
• Rust语言设计中基本类型的合理性和早期决策的长期影响。

data.title: From Clocks to Chaos: The Rhythms of Life
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary: 《From Clocks to Chaos》是由生理学领域的两名杰出研究者Leon Glass和Michael Mackey所著，探讨了生理节律的核心理论问题，如节律的生成、启动与停止、扰动影响以及空间中的振荡组织等。该书面向生物科学家、医生、物理学家和数学家，且不要求读者具备高级数学知识。书中特别讨论了“动态疾病”，即非病原体感染导致的疾病，而是由基本生理功能时间异常引起。该书为理解生理学中的动态过程提供了坚实基础。售价83美元/70英镑，平装本和电子书均有50%折扣。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Leon Glass的论文及其参与创建的PhysioNet数据库的意义和性质

不同观点：
• [teleforce] 的观点：teleforce认为Leon Glass的论文《Synchronization and rhythmic processes in physiology》是一项重要的科学贡献，并强调Glass参与了建立MIT-BIH PhysioNet数据库的工作。teleforce通过引用相关文献[1][2]来支持他的观点，指出Glass在复杂生理信号研究资源中的贡献。

• [bravesoul2] 的观点：bravesoul2对Glass的研究是否与伪科学有关提出质疑，通过引用维基百科上关于生物节律（Biorhythm）的条目[https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biorhythm_(pseudoscience)]，将Glass的研究与伪科学进行对比，质疑其科学性。

补充讨论：
• teleforce提供的文献[1]和[2]显示了Glass在生理同步和节律过程方面的科学研究，以及其参与创建的PhysioNet数据库在生理信号研究中的重要性。
• bravesoul2的评论引发了关于Glass研究是否涉及伪科学的讨论，这涉及到科学研究与伪科学之间的区分问题。
• 争议的焦点在于Glass的研究内容是否与伪科学相关，这需要进一步了解Glass的具体研究方法和成果来做出判断。

总结：评论主要围绕Leon Glass的科学贡献及其研究是否涉及伪科学展开讨论。teleforce支持Glass的学术贡献，而bravesoul2则提出质疑，引发对研究性质的进一步探讨。

In an important new contribution to the literature of chaos, two distinguished researchers in the field of physiology probe central theoretical questions about physiological rhythms. Topics discussed include: How are rhythms generated? How do they start and stop? What are the effects of perturbation of the rhythms? How are oscillations organized in space? Leon Glass and Michael Mackey address an audience of biological scientists, physicians, physical scientists, and mathematicians, but the work assumes no knowledge of advanced mathematics.
Variation of rhythms outside normal limits, or appearance of new rhythms where none existed previously, are associated with disease. One of the most interesting features of the book is that it makes a start at explaining “dynamical diseases” that are not the result of infection by pathogens but that stem from abnormalities in the timing of essential functions. From Clocks to Chaos provides a firm foundation for understanding dynamic processes in physiology.

data.title: Progressive JSON
data.author: kacesensitive
data.article_summary: 这篇文章提出了“渐进式JSON”的概念，类似于渐进式JPEG图片的加载方式。传统JSON必须等到所有数据传输完成后才能解析和使用，而渐进式JSON旨在通过流式传输让客户端逐步接收和处理数据。文章讨论了简单的流式解析的问题，如数据不完整和类型不匹配，导致难以使用。为了解决这些问题，文章提出了一种广度优先的传输方法，使用占位符逐步填充数据，这样即使某部分数据生成较慢，也不会阻碍其他部分的传输和显示。这种方法可以提高传输效率，避免因单一部分延迟而影响整体加载。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于"Progressive JSON"的可行性、用途及其实现方式的讨论

不同观点：
• **支持并扩展Progressive JSON概念**：
  - **goranmoomin**：认为文章是在解释React Server Components如何通过类似JSON的格式传输组件树，允许React显示加载中的占位符，从而提高加载速度。
  - **xelxebar**：进一步提出该方法可应用于任何树状数据结构，并建议通过发送表头和类型信息，然后分批传输数据向量，以优化加载时间。
  - **polyomino**：分享了在音频和视觉应用中的类似经验，指出音频可以逐步播放，而视觉数据则需要完全解析后才能显示。

• **质疑Progressive JSON的必要性**：
  - **Velorivox**：认为大多数应用不需要如此复杂的解决方案，通过多次调用即可解决加载问题。
  - **slt2021**：建议直接压缩JSON文件，而不是在错误的抽象层次上解决假问题。
  - **turtlebits**：认为Progressive JSON像是为JS bundle过大而引入的额外复杂性，质疑其必要性。

• **提出替代方案**：
  - **jarym**：认为使用类似行分隔JSON和JSON Patch的方法更容易理解和处理增量更新。
  - **roxolotl**：指出这与JSON API链接类似，可以作为前端处理这些链接的实现方式。
  - **aljow**：认为如果JSON需要如此复杂地处理，那它可能不是合适的格式，建议重新设计。

• **技术实现讨论**：
  - **bob1029**：提到.NET中的Utf8JsonReader可以实现类似的流式JSON解析。
  - **KronisLV**：建议从数据库查询开始优化，以确定返回对象的顺序，并逐步传递数据。
  - **yen223**：指出常见的树序列化方式多为深度优先，并分析了广度优先序列化的挑战。

• **API设计建议**：
  - **jimmcslim**：提到GraphQL曾经试图解决类似问题，但似乎已经不再流行。
  - **nixpulves**：建议在API规范中加入延迟要求，以帮助确定哪些内容应被内联。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及了多种技术方法，包括JSON Patch、JSON API链接、JSON行分隔（jsonl）等，显示出社区对不同解决方案的兴趣和经验。
- 争议的焦点在于Progressive JSON是否过度复杂化了解决方案，以及是否有更简单有效的替代方法。

44147945.article_content:
Progressive JSON
May 31, 2025
Pay what you like
Do you know about Progressive JPEGs? Here’s a
nice explanation
of what a Progressive JPEG is. The idea is that instead of loading the image top to bottom, the image instead is fuzzy at first and then progressively becomes more crisp.
What if we apply the same idea to transferring JSON?
Suppose you have a JSON tree with some data:
{
header:
'
Welcome to my blog
'
,
post:
{
content:
'
This is my article
'
,
comments:
[
'
First comment
'
,
'
Second comment
'
,
// ...
]
},
footer:
'
Hope you like it
'
}
Now imagine you want to transfer it over the wire. Because the format is JSON, you’re not going to have a valid object tree until the last byte loads. You have to wait for the
entire
thing to load, then call
JSON.parse
, and then process it.
The client can’t do
anything
with JSON until the server sends the
last
byte. If a part of the JSON was slow to generate on the server (e.g. loading
comments
took a slow database trip),
the client can’t
start any
work until the server
finishes all
the work.
Would you call that good engineering? And yet it’s the status quo—that’s how 99.9999%
*
of apps send and process JSON. Do we dare to improve on that?
* I made it up
Streaming JSON
We can try to improve this by implementing a
streaming
JSON parser. A streaming JSON parser would be able to produce an object tree from an incomplete input:
{
header:
'
Welcome to my blog
'
,
post:
{
content:
'
This is my article
'
,
comments:
[
'
First comment
'
,
'
Second comment
'
If you ask for the result at this point, a streaming parser would hand you this:
{
header:
'
Welcome to my blog
'
,
post:
{
content:
'
This is my article
'
,
comments:
[
'
First comment
'
,
'
Second comment
'
// (The rest of the comments are missing)
]
}
// (The footer property is missing)
}
However, this isn’t too great either.
One downside of this approach is that the objects are kind of malformed. For example, the top-level object was supposed to have three properties (
header
,
post
, and
footer
), but the
footer
is missing because it hasn’t appeared in the stream yet. The
post
was supposed to have three
comments
, but you
can’t actually tell
whether more
comments
are coming or if this was the last one.
In a way, this is inherent to streaming—didn’t we
want
to get incomplete data?—but
this makes it very difficult to actually
use
this data on the client.
None of the types “match up” due to missing fields. We don’t know what’s complete and what’s not. That’s why streaming JSON isn’t popular aside from niche use cases. It’s just too hard to actually take advantage of it in the application logic which generally assumes the types are correct, “ready” means “complete”, and so on.
In the analogy with JPEG, this naïve approach to streaming matches the default “top-down” loading mechanism. The picture you see is crisp but you only see the top 10%. So despite the high fidelity, you don’t actually see
what’s
on the picture.
Curiously, this is also how streaming
HTML itself
works by default. If you load an HTML page on a slow connection, it will be streamed in the document order:
<
html
>
<
body
>
<
header
>
Welcome to my blog
</
header
>
<
article
>
<
p
>
This is my article
</
p
>
<
ul
class=
"
comments
"
>
<
li
>
First comment
</
li
>
<
li
>
Second comment
</
li
>
This has some upsides—the browser is able to display the page partially—but it has the same issues. The cutoff point is arbitrary and can be visually jarring or even mess up the page layout. It’s unclear if more content is coming. Whatever’s below—like the footer—is cut off, even if it
was
ready on the server and
could
have been sent earlier. When we stream data
in order
,
one slow part delays
everything
.
Let’s repeat that: when we stream things in order they appear, a
single
slow part delays
everything
that comes after it. Can you think of some way to fix this?
Progressive JSON
There is another way to approach streaming.
So far we’ve been sending things
depth-first
. We start with the top-level object’s properties, we go into that object’s
post
property, then we go into
that
object’s
comments
property, and so on. If something is slow, everything else gets held up.
However, we could also send data
breadth-first
.
Suppose we send the top-level object like this:
{
header:
"
$1
"
,
post:
"
$2
"
,
footer:
"
$3
"
}
Here,
"$1"
,
"$2"
,
"$3"
refer to pieces of information that
have not been sent yet
. These are placeholders that can progressively be filled in later in the stream.
For example, suppose the server sends a few more rows of data to the stream:
{
header:
"
$1
"
,
post:
"
$2
"
,
footer:
"
$3
"
}
/* $1 */
"
Welcome to my blog
"
/* $3 */
"
Hope you like it
"
Notice that we’re not obligated to send the rows in any particular order. In the above example, we’ve just sent both
$1
and
$3
—but the
$2
row is still pending!

header:

44147945.article_summary: 这篇文章提出了“渐进式JSON”的概念，类似于渐进式JPEG图片的加载方式。传统JSON必须等到所有数据传输完成后才能解析和使用，而渐进式JSON旨在通过流式传输让客户端逐步接收和处理数据。文章讨论了简单的流式解析的问题，如数据不完整和类型不匹配，导致难以使用。为了解决这些问题，文章提出了一种广度优先的传输方法，使用占位符逐步填充数据，这样即使某部分数据生成较慢，也不会阻碍其他部分的传输和显示。这种方法可以提高传输效率，避免因单一部分延迟而影响整体加载。

data.author: timthorn

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电动垂直起降（eVTOL）飞行器的设计、功能及其应用前景

不同观点：
• **FabHK**：认为固定翼与旋翼结合的VTOL设计比复杂的旋转变翼机制（如Lilium公司的设计）更安全和高效。他对飞行中能否从垂直起降模式平滑过渡到固定翼飞行模式表示不确定，但总体上看好这种设计。

• **JSR_FDED**：对这种结合电动、VTOL和传统固定翼飞行的设计表示不解，认为这是一个过于小众的创新，并请求其他人解释其重要性。

• **choult**：提到Kemble这个地方，通过描述周围环境（起伏的山丘和田野，以及突然出现的747飞机）间接暗示了对不同飞行器（包括VTOL和传统飞机）共同使用的兴趣或惊讶。

• **ikekkdcjkfke**：关注飞行器的安全性，特别是单个齿轮故障是否会导致整个飞行器坠毁。随后编辑补充说，因为有固定翼设计，飞行器可以在紧急情况下滑翔着陆，从而提高安全性。

• **bigtones**：对一架VTOL飞行器没有进行垂直起飞表示讽刺，认为这是一个不显著的进展，暗示对该技术实际应用的怀疑。

• **kkfx**：提出eVTOL并不适合城市应用，而是适用于分散居住的地区，并通过引用多个链接和文件支持其观点。他还讨论了社会对eVTOL和绿色新政（Green New Deal）的接受度问题，认为公众尚未理解这种飞行器的实际应用场景。

补充讨论：
- eVTOL飞行器的设计安全性及其实际应用场景是讨论的核心，特别是其能否在故障时安全着陆。
- 不同用户对eVTOL技术的实际意义和应用前景存在分歧，一些人看好其效率和安全性，另一些人则对其应用场景和创新性表示怀疑。
- kkfx的评论特别提到了eVTOL与绿色新政的关联，拓宽了讨论的范围，涉及到城市与分散居住模式的资源消耗问题。

主要讨论点：社区工具共享和租赁网站的潜力和挑战

不同观点：

   - [SamBam] 认为工具共享可以减少消费，促进资源共享，尤其在密集城市环境中非常有意义。
   - [pruetj] 表示DIY趋势正在增长，通过租赁工具可以避免不必要的购买和储存问题，支持工具租赁业务的想法。

   - [ttecho] 指出公共图书馆的工具租赁质量和种类有限，认为该理念有扩展空间。

• **商业模式探讨**：
   - [bryanrasmussen] 提出在特定社区设立工具中心并由专人管理，公司可以通过工具分发和租赁业务 disrupting 传统五金行业，并提到该模式在欧洲的潜在应用。
   - [pruetj] 认为个人工具租赁市场有潜力，特别是在一些不常用工具上，可以通过小额租赁避免购买和储存问题。

• **法律和安全问题**：
   - [tlavoie] 提到设立工具图书馆需要考虑成本、耗材、责任和借用者教育等问题，特别是涉及电动工具时的安全问题。

   - [tomcam] 和 [heyhuy] 担心工具损坏或欺诈行为，特别是当责任方拒绝承认问题时。

   - [angry_moose] 和 [pants2] 都对网站的导航设计提出批评，认为初次访问者可能感到困惑，建议将租赁功能放在显眼位置。
   - [StrandedKitty] 提到网站的视觉设计问题，特别是导航栏的对比度和可见性。

补充讨论：
• **欺诈和盗窃防范**：
   - [heyhuy] 和 [nothercastle] 都提到如何防止欺诈和盗窃是一个关键问题，可能需要工具拥有者自行保护其财产。
   
• **市场规模和网络效应**：
   - [satvikpendem] 提到该模式需要一定的网络效应才能有效运作，并幽默询问当前用户数量。

争议焦点：
• 工具租赁和共享中的法律责任和安全问题是主要争议点，特别是如何处理工具损坏、欺诈和盗窃问题。
• 网站设计和用户体验的优化也是讨论中的一个重要方面，特别是如何让用户更容易理解和使用租赁功能。

data.title: New adaptive optics shows details of our star's atmosphere
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 科学家开发了一种新的“日冕自适应光学系统”，首次拍摄到太阳日冕层的最清晰图像和视频。该系统安装在美国新泽西理工学院运营的1.6米Goode太阳望远镜上，能够消除地球大气湍流造成的图像模糊。这些高分辨率图像展示了日冕中精细结构的快速变化，包括日珥的重组和等离子体流的形成与崩溃，还首次清晰捕捉到“日冕雨”现象，即冷却的等离子体凝结后落回太阳表面。这些观测为研究日冕加热、太阳爆发和空间天气提供了新的视角，并可能带来更多科学发现。

“Raindrops in the Sun’s Corona”: New Adaptive Optics Shows Stunning Details of our Star’s Atmosphere
Credit: Schmidt et al./NJIT/NSO/AURA/NSF
Home
»
“Raindrops in the Sun’s Corona”: New Adaptive Optics Shows Stunning Details of our Star’s Atmosphere
Release Date:
May 27, 2025
Scientists from the U.S. National Science Foundation National Solar Observatory and New Jersey Institute of Technology produced the finest images of the Sun’s corona to date. To make these high-resolution images and movies, the team developed a new ‘coronal adaptive optics’ system that removes blur from images caused by the Earth’s atmosphere. Their ground-breaking results were recently published in Nature Astronomy and pave the way for deeper insight into coronal heating, solar eruptions, and space weather, and open an opportunity for new discoveries in the Sun’s atmosphere.
Scientists develop new optical system that removes blur over fine-structure in the Sun’s corona, revealing clearest images to date
BOULDER, CO, Tuesday, May 27, 2025
–
The Sun’s corona—the outermost layer of its atmosphere, visible only during a total solar eclipse—has long intrigued scientists due to its extreme temperatures, violent eruptions, and large prominences. However, turbulence in the Earth’s atmosphere has caused image blur and hindered observations of the corona. A ground-breaking recent development by scientists from the U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF) National Solar Observatory (NSO), and New Jersey Institute of Technology (NJIT), is changing that by using adaptive optics to remove the blur.
As published in
Nature Astronomy
, this pioneering ‘coronal adaptive optics’ technology has produced the most astonishing, clearest images and videos of fine-structure in the corona to date. This development will open the door for deeper insights into the corona’s enigmatic behavior and the processes driving space weather.
Most Detailed Coronal Images to Date Revealed
Funded by the NSF and installed at the 1.6-meter Goode Solar Telescope (GST), operated by NJIT’s Center for Solar-Terrestrial Research (CSTR) at Big Bear Solar Observatory (BBSO) in California, “Cona”—the adaptive optics system responsible for these new images—compensates for the blur caused by air turbulence in the Earth’s atmosphere —similar to the bumpy air passengers feel during a flight.
“The turbulence in the air severely degrades images of objects in space, like our Sun, seen through our telescopes. But we can correct for that,”
says Dirk Schmidt, NSO Adaptive Optics Scientist who led the development.
Among the team’s remarkable observations is a movie of a quickly restructuring solar prominence unveiling fine, turbulent internal flows. Solar prominences are large, bright features, often appearing as arches or loops, extending outward from the Sun’s surface.
https://nso.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Prominence-1-Video.mp4
This image of a prominence above the solar surface is a snapshot of a 4-minute time-lapse movie that reveals its rapid, fine, and turbulent restructuring with unprecedented detail. The Sun’s fluffy-looking surface is covered by “spicules”, short-lived plasma jets, whose creation is still the subject of scientific debate. The streaks on the right of this image are coronal rain falling down onto the Sun’s surface. This image was taken by the Goode Solar Telescope at Big Bear Solar Observatory using the new coronal adaptive optics system Cona. The image shows the hydrogen-alpha light emitted by the solar plasma. The image is artificially colorized, yet based on the color of hydrogen-alpha light, and darker color is brighter light. Credit: Schmidt et al./NJIT/NSO/AURA/NSF
A second movie replays the rapid formation and collapse of a finely structured plasma stream.
“These are by far the most detailed observations of this kind, showing features not previously observed, and it’s not quite clear what they are,”
says Vasyl Yurchyshyn, co-author of the study and NJIT-CSTR research professor. “
It is super exciting to build an instrument that shows us the Sun like never before,
” Schmidt adds.
https://nso.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Plasmoid-Video.mp4
This image was taken by the Goode Solar Telescope at Big Bear Solar Observatory using the new coronal adaptive optics system Cona. The image shows the hydrogen-alpha light emitted by the solar plasma. The image is artificially colorized, yet based on the color of hydrogen-alpha light, and darker color is brighter light.
Credit:
Schmidt et al./NJIT/NSO/AURA/NSF
A third movie shows fine strands of coronal rain—a phenomenon where cooling plasma condenses and falls back toward the Sun’s surface. “
Raindrops in the Sun’s corona can be narrower than 20 kilometers,”
NSO Astronomer Thomas Schad concludes from the most detailed images of coronal rain to date, “
These findings offer new invaluable observational insight that is vital to test computer models of coronal processes.
”
https://nso.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Coronal-Rain-Vi

data.title: Oniux: Kernel-level Tor isolation for any Linux app
data.author: marcodiego
data.article_summary:
**摘要：**

文章介绍了一款名为 **oniux** 的小型命令行工具，它通过 Linux 命名空间为任何 Linux 应用程序提供 Tor 网络隔离。oniux 使用内核提供的隔离功能，将应用程序置于独立的网络命名空间中，并通过自定义网络接口路由流量，确保数据不会泄露。与传统的 torsocks 相比，oniux 更安全，因为它不依赖于动态链接的 libc，且能防止恶意应用程序泄露数据。oniux 需要在 Linux 系统上安装 Rust 工具链，并通过克隆系统调用创建隔离的子进程。用户可以通过简单的命令行操作实现应用的 Tor 隔离，例如 `oniux curl https://example.com`。

**关键特性：**
- 使用 Linux 命名空间实现隔离。
- 比 torsocks 更安全，防止数据泄露。
- 支持隔离整个 shell 和图形应用程序。
- 基于 Arti 和 onionmasq，用 Rust 编写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Oniux工具的功能、使用方法、安全性及其与其他工具的比较

不同观点：
• **mike-cardwell** 认为 Oniux 的工作原理与 torsocks 不同，即使在本地 Tor 守护进程停止后，Oniux 仍然可以工作，而 torsocks 和 torify 则不行。他还提到 Oniux 可以在 Docker 中运行，但需要使用 `--privileged` 参数。此外，他指出了 Oniux 安装说明中的版本号错误，应将 0.4.0 改为 0.5.0。

• **mjg59** 提到十年前曾与一位Tor开发者讨论过类似话题，当时网络命名空间还是新概念。反馈指出，这种方式容易让用户误以为自己在安全地使用Tor，但实际上可能会泄露可识别信息，因此没有进一步推进。

• **natmaka** 质疑 Oniux 的保护范围是否仅限于TCP流量，并询问如何保护非TCP活动。

• **tobias2014** 将 Oniux 与 Orjail 进行比较，指出 Orjail 虽然四年未更新但仍有效，且提供与 firejail 结合使用的额外隔离功能，而 Oniux 目前没有类似功能。

• **ahmedfromtunis** 询问是否可以通过 Oniux 使用 Chrome 访问 Tor 网站。

• **ericfrederich** 担心 Oniux 进程是否会使用用户的配置，进而泄露IRC用户名或浏览器cookies，尤其是在配置未更改的情况下。

• **alfiedotwtf** 赞赏 Oniux 的开发体验（DevEx），认为其设计对新手非常友好，并对开发团队表示感谢。

• **hexo** 建议将 Oniux 的原型用 C 语言重写，才会考虑使用。

补充讨论：
• 用户对 Oniux 的功能、配置和安全性存在不同程度的关注和疑虑。
• 对 Oniux 与类似工具（如 Orjail）的比较也是一个讨论重点，特别是在功能和隔离能力方面。
• 安装说明中的版本号错误是一个具体的操作问题，用户提供了修正方法。
• 不同用户对开发体验和工具实现语言有各自的偏好和建议。

争议焦点：
• Oniux 的安全性和隐私保护能力受到质疑，尤其是与用户配置和数据泄露相关的问题。
• Oniux 与其他工具（如 Orjail）在功能上的差距和优势是比较的焦点。

Introducing oniux: Kernel-level Tor isolation for any Linux app
by
cve
| May 14, 2025
When launching privacy-critical apps and services, developers want to make sure that every packet really only goes through Tor. One mistyped proxy settingâor a single system-call outside the SOCKS wrapperâand your data is suddenly on the line.
That's why today, we are excited to introduce
oniux
: a small command-line utility providing Tor network isolation for third-party applications using Linux namespaces. Built on Arti, and onionmasq, oniux drop-ships any Linux program into its own network namespace to route it through Tor and strips away the potential for data leaks. If your work, activism, or research demands rock-solid traffic isolation, oniux delivers it.
What are Linux namespaces? ð§
Namespaces are an isolation feature found in the Linux kernel that were introduced around the year 2000. They provide a secure way of isolating a certain part of an application from the rest of the system. Namespaces come in various forms and shapes. Some examples include network namespaces, mount namespaces, process namespaces, and a few more; each of them isolating a certain amount of system resources from an application.
What do we mean by
system resources
? In Linux, system resources are available globally by all applications on the system. The most notable example of this is probably your operating system clock, but there are many other areas as well, such as the list of all processes, the file system, and the list of users.
Namespaces
containerize
a certain part of an application from the rest of the operating system; this is exactly what Docker uses in order to provide its isolation primitives.
Tor + Namespaces = â¤ï¸
As outlined above, namespaces are a powerful feature that gives us the ability to isolate Tor network access of an arbitrary application. We put each application in a network namespace that doesn't provide access to system-wide network interfaces (such as eth0), and instead provides a custom network interface onion0.
This allows us to isolate an arbitrary application over Tor in the most secure way possible software-wise, namely by relying on a security primitive offered by the operating system kernel. Unlike SOCKS, the application cannot accidentally leak data by failing to make some connection via the configured SOCKS, which may happen due to a mistake by the developer.
oniux vs. torsocks
You may have also heard of a tool with a similar goal, known as
torsocks
, which works by
overwriting all network-related libc functions in a way to route traffic over a
SOCKS proxy offered by Tor.  While this approach is a bit more cross-platform,
it has the notable downside that applications making system calls
not
through
a dynamically linked libc, either with malicious intent or not, will leak data.
Most notably, this excludes support for purely static binaries and applications
from the Zig ecosystem.
The following provides a basic comparison on
oniux
vs
torsocks
:
oniux
torsocks
Standalone application
Requires running Tor daemon
Uses Linux namespaces
Uses an ld.so preload hack
Works on all applications
Only works on applications making system calls through libc
Malicious application cannot leak
Malicious application can leak by making a system call through raw assembly
Linux only
Cross-platform
New and experimental
Battle-proven for over 15 years
Uses Arti as its engine
Uses CTor as its engine
Written in Rust
Written in C
How can I use
oniux
? ð§
First, you need a Linux system with a Rust toolchain installed.
Afterwards, you can install
oniux
with the following command:
$ cargo install --git https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/core/oniux oniux@0.4.0
Once that is done, you are ready to go for using
oniux
!  ð
Using
oniux
is straightforward:
# Perform a simple HTTPS query using oniux!
$ oniux curl https://icanhazip.com
<A TOR EXIT NODE IP ADDRESS>
# oniux also supports IPv6 of course!
$ oniux curl -6 https://ipv6.icanhazip.com
<A TOR EXIT NODE IPv6 ADDRESS>
# Tor without onion services is like a car without an engine ...
$ oniux curl http://2gzyxa5ihm7nsggfxnu52rck2vv4rvmdlkiu3zzui5du4xyclen53wid.onion/index.html
# You can also enable logging if you are a nerd. ð¤
$
RUST_LOG
=
debug oniux curl https://icanhazip.com
# If you want, you can "torify" your entire shell, isolating all processes within!
$ oniux bash
# If you are in a desktop environment, you can isolate graphical applications too!
$ oniux hexchat
How does this work internally? âï¸
oniux
works by immediately spawning a child process using the
clone(2)
system call, which is isolated in its own network, mount, PID, and user
namespace.  This process then mounts its own copy of
/proc
followed by UID
and GID mappings to the respective UID and GID of the parent process.
Afterwards, it creates a temporary file with nameserver entries which will then
be bind mounted onto
/etc/resolv.conf

- 支持隔离整个 shell 和图形应用程序。
- 基于 Arti 和 onionmasq，用 Rust 编写。

data.title: Plutonium Powered Pacemaker (From 1974)
data.author: BafS
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了1974年使用的钚动力心脏起搏器。这种起搏器采用含2至4居里钚-238的温差电池作为电源，利用钚衰变产生的热量发电，以刺激心脏保持规律跳动。美国目前仍有50至100人使用这种核动力起搏器。当患者去世后，起搏器需被取出并送至洛斯阿拉莫斯国家实验室回收钚。起搏器的电子元件嵌入环氧树脂中，外壳由钛制成，能抵御枪击和火化等极端情况。起搏器表面辐射剂量为每小时5至15毫雷姆，患者每年全身暴露量约为0.1雷姆，其配偶则为7.5毫雷姆。该设备由Cordis、Medtronic和Coratomic三家公司生产，直径约2.75英寸，由洛斯阿拉莫斯国家实验室捐赠。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对使用Pu-238作为能源的早期心脏起搏器的技术细节、历史背景及其相关成本的讨论

不同观点：
• [acidburnNSA] 认为Pu-238提供的年辐射剂量（0.1 rem）较低，仅为普通人每年背景辐射的1/6左右，并指出Pu-238与用于核链式反应的Pu-239不同，强调其安全性。此外，提到Pu-238用于太空探测器和火星车的能源。

• [jandrewrogers] 对心脏起搏器的辐射来源提出质疑，指出Pu-238的衰变链主要通过α射线发射，理论上不会产生能够穿透起搏器外壳的γ射线和中子，因此对辐射来源表示困惑。

• [anovikov] 关注Pu-238的成本，指出以当前价格计算，这种材料的成本高达14,000美元，暗示这种技术在经济上可能不具备可持续性。

• [xattt] 对该技术的编程方式表示兴趣，推测可能有外部设备用于设定参数，关注该技术的实现方式而非材料本身。

补充讨论：
• [sanarothe] 提供了进一步阅读的资源链接，推荐David Prutchi关于心脏起搏器和神经刺激器历史的综合资料，涵盖从早期原子设计到现代设备的发展历程，提供了历史背景补充。

争议焦点：Pu-238在心脏起搏器中的辐射安全性及其来源的科学性是讨论中的争议点，[jandrewrogers] 对辐射类型的科学解释与 [acidburnNSA] 的安全性描述形成对比。

44146847.article_content:
Plutonium Powered Pacemaker (1974)
Pacemakers are used to stimulate a regular heartbeat when the body's natural electrical pacing system is irregular or not transmitting properly.
Over the years, various power sources have been used for pacemakers, including thermoelectric batteries containing 2 to 4 curies of plutonium-238 (88 year half-life). As the term "thermoelectric" implies, the heat from the decaying plutonium is used to generate the electricity that stimulates the heart. At present (2003), there are between 50 and 100 people in the U.S. who have nuclear powered pacemakers. When one of these individuals dies, the pacemaker is supposed to be removed and shipped to Los Alamos where the plutonium will be recovered.
The pacemaker shown in these photos, produced by Medtronic, has had its plutonium removed.
As can be seen in the above photo, the unit's electronics are embedded in epoxy. The hard titanium case is designed to withstand any credible event including gunshots and cremation.
Dose rates at the surface of the pacemaker are approximately 5 to 15 mrem per hour from the emitted gamma rays and neutrons. The whole-body exposure is estimated to be approximately 0.1 rem per year to the patient and approximately 7.5 mrem per year to the patient's spouse.
Three U.S. companies manufactured these devices: the Cordis Corporation, Medtronic Inc. and Coratomic Inc.
Size: ca. 2.75" in diameter.
Donated by the Los Alamos National Laboratory Source Recovery Program.
References
National Council on Radiation Protection and Measurements. NCRP Report No. 95. Radiation Exposure of the US Population from Consumer Products and Miscellaneous Sources. 1987.
William Kolb and Paul Frame. Living With Radiation: the First Hundred Years. Third Ed. Syntec Inc. 2002.

data.title: Show HN: Open-source P2P file transfer
data.author: goodpanda
data.article_summary: Berb是一个简化的P2P文件共享平台，采用隐私优先的设计。它利用WebRTC技术，无需服务器或上传文件，直接在设备间传输文件，确保安全和快速。主要特点包括通过WebRTC数据通道直接连接用户，文件不经过服务器。当前开发任务包括网络断开自动重连、多文件支持以及在支持的浏览器上保存流。贡献代码前需先开启一个讨论。技术栈包括Node.js、JavaScript、WebRTC、P2P和Pug。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Iroh's Sendme 项目的技术细节、安全性及其替代方案

不同观点：
• [satvikpendem] 提出了对 Iroh's Sendme 项目的关注，并分享了项目链接，表明对该项目的兴趣。
• [howtofly] 认为信令服务器可能成为中间人攻击的理想位置，并指出项目的README文件未提及如何解决这一安全问题。
• [ranger_danger] 提到尽管项目声称"无服务器"，但由于对称NAT或CGNAT的广泛存在，许多用户仍需要TURN服务器来实现P2P连接，并表示自己从未成功使用类似p2p/WebRTC的网站。
• [fabrice_d] 关心ICE协议的offer/answer交换过程是否通过用户服务器上的WebSocket实现，询问该项目的具体技术实现方式。
• [pwn0] 对项目的开源许可和贡献指南提出建议，希望项目添加相关信息以方便他人参与。
• [opengears] 提到该项目的替代方案，推荐了LocalSend作为另一个类似工具。
• [evbogue] 探讨了浏览器直接连接的技术挑战，特别是NAT穿透的问题，并分享了一个相关工具（Trystero），认为该领域需要更多研究。

补充讨论：
• 安全性是讨论的焦点之一，尤其是信令服务器可能带来的MITM攻击风险。
• NAT和CGNAT对P2P连接的影响也被多次提及，表明这是实际应用中的一个主要障碍。
• 不同用户分享了其他相关工具和项目，显示出对类似技术方案的广泛兴趣和需求。

data.title: Toxic Proteins for Drug Discovery
data.author: mailyk
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了有毒蛋白质和肽在药物研发中的潜力。这些有毒分子最初是物种间冲突中的“分子武器”，但通过研究其作用机制，科学家可以将其转化为有益的药物。文章提到，许多有毒的氨基酸、肽和蛋白质来自生物的防御或攻击机制，它们能够引起疼痛、麻痹甚至死亡。然而，经过安全性的改进，这些毒素可以成为有效的治疗手段，例如肉毒杆菌毒素（Botox）已被用于医学美容。随着小分子药物的发展，基于氨基酸的治疗方法正变得越来越重要，尤其是来自动物毒液的毒素，预计将成为下一代药物的重要来源。文章还提到，像Wegovy和Ozempic这样的肽类药物虽未直接模仿毒液分子，但利用了毒素的天然作用机制，展示了自然界“有毒蛋白质”在药物开发中的持续启发作用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GLP-1类似药物（如semaglutide）的来源及其启示

不同观点：
• [JSR_FDED] 认为semaglutide作为当前热门的治疗肽类药物，其灵感来源于大自然，特别是从吉拉毒蜥的毒液中首次发现类似GLP-1激素的作用。该评论者对大自然作为“研发实验室”的概念表示惊叹，并将自然选择和进化过程比喻为数十亿年运行的实验。

补充讨论：
• 评论提到semaglutide等GLP-1药物的研发受到自然界生物的启发，特别是吉拉毒蜥能够在恶劣环境中长时间不吃东西，保持低代谢和血糖水平，这为药物研发提供了宝贵的线索。
• 评论者用幽默的语气指出，大自然提供了“数十种新的死亡方式”，暗示自然界中潜在的危险和不可预测性，但同时也暗含了对自然作为创新源泉的敬畏。
• 争议焦点可能在于如何更好地利用自然界的资源进行科学研究和药物开发，尤其是在尊重自然和可持续发展的前提下。
